articles.title: Samsung’s wider Z Fold 8 feels just right
articles.summary: But $1,900 is a hell of a lot for the Galaxy Z Fold 8, a phone with no telephoto camera.
articles.body: A year after overhauling its Z Fold phone with a radically thinner design, Samsung has changed things up again, this time altering the shape entirely. The Z Fold 8 is wider than any of Samsung’s previous foldables, and shorter too, a size and shape somewhere between Samsung’s traditional Flip and Fold models. In photos, I wasn’t impressed by the squat shape. In person, to my surprise, it feels great, and almost immediately intuitive. If you want to get a feel for it yourself, grab your passport — the Z Fold 8 is about the same height and less than half an inch more narrow. This isn’t Samsung’s only new foldable this year, and in fact, its lineup just got more confusing. The Z Fold 8 may be the official follow-up to last year’s impressive Z Fold 7, but in truth the Z Fold 8 Ultra is the straightforward sequel. That phone has the same squarish inner screen as previous Z Fold phones and a similar triple rear camera. The name feels like a sly trick to get around this year’s inevitable price hikes: Samsung slapped “Ultra” on the box of its highest-end model to help cover for pricing the phone at $2,099.99, up $100 from the Z Fold 7. Meanwhile, with its wider screens and stripped back cameras, the Z Fold 8 feels less like a sequel and more like a spinoff. And it almost — almost — looks like a bargain at $1,899.99, down $100 on its nominal predecessor. [Image: The Z Fold 8 sits right in between Samsung’s other two new foldables in size. Samsung isn’t the first to the Z Fold 8’s form factor. Huawei’s Pura X Max launched in April with a similar shape, though it’s only available in China. Apple is widely expected to be next, using a similar passport-esque shape for its first iPhone foldable in September. In truth, elements of this design are even older: The Fold 8 is almost exactly the same width as Google’s first-gen Pixel Fold, though a good deal shorter, bringing foldable phones full circle. I’ve been skeptical about the return of the wider foldable, which in photos looks squat and uncomfortable, too wide to use naturally while closed and too short to feel expansive when open. The industry tried this design once and moved on, so why — other than Apple’s potential adoption — should we give it a go again? Samsung’s answer is that its two Z Fold 8 models are designed for different users and different uses. The Z Fold 8 Ultra, tall and thin when closed and similar to a square when open, is meant to be a multitasking monster, useful for running apps in split-screen, giving you the equivalent screen space of two regular 6.5-inch phones side by side. The wider Z Fold 8 is instead about consumption: Its 4:3 aspect ratio is equally natural for watching Netflix shows in landscape as it is for reading ebooks in portrait, and at 201g, it’s light enough to hold comfortably in one hand. Or, as Samsung’s marketing department puts it, the Fold 8 is for “joy-maxxing,” and the Ultra is for “power-maxxing.” I sit through these presentations so that you don’t have to, folks. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The 4:3 display isn’t widescreen, so you’ll still get letterboxing at the top and bottom when watching most videos, whether on YouTube or a streaming service. But unlike Samsung’s previous squarish Folds, which weren’t much wider than simply turning your phone on its side, opening the Z Fold 8 up really does fit more video onto your screen, and the wider aspect ratio will be much more natural for gaming too. It feels less like a foldable and more like a tablet and is all the better for it. I’m still a little uncertain whether I like how the Z Fold 8 feels closed — the way I use foldables the majority of the time. The width of the 10:16 cover display is less noticeable than I expected, and I got used to using the phone this way remarkably quickly, but I’m worried it might feel less comfortable if you stick the phone in a case. The reduced height proves an unexpected blessing here, making it easier and more comfortable to stretch across the screen one-handed than on larger slab phones like the S26 Ultra. A lot will depend on how well apps adapt to the shorter screen, though Samsung has already announced that Instagram is on board with optimizations. [Image: Closed, it’s short and wide, but feels more comfortable than I expected. There are other considerations to the Fold 8 than its new shape. The Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset, optimized together with Samsung, makes this about as powerful as any other flagship out there. The 120Hz OLED main display is the same in specs as the Fold 8 Ultra’s, including an impressive peak brightness of 3,000 nits and a new anti-reflective coating to reduce glare. It supports the same new software features as the Z Fold 8 Ultra, including the official launch of Gemini Intelligence task automation and a proactive AI feature called Now Nudge that pops up with cross-app suggestions to add an event to your calendar or send someone an email. For the first time, Samsung has caught up with its Chinese competition and adopted silicon-carbon batteries, a new type of lithium ion cell that incorporates a small amount of silicon alongside the graphite in the anode. Silicon-carbon batteries can squeeze higher capacities into smaller spaces, but they come with a downside: The highly reactive silicon is less stable, and there are fears that silicon-carbon batteries will lose capacity more quickly over time. The 4,800mAh battery capacity of the Fold 8 isn’t an enormous jump from the 4,400mAh in the Fold 7 and pales in comparison to the biggest foldable battery around, Honor’s 6,660mAh Magic V6. A cautious approach to silicon-carbon is understandable from Samsung, which still bears the scars of the disastrous Galaxy Note 7 battery, which prompted a full recall of that phone in 2016 over safety concerns. “Silicon-carbon cells must be carefully managed,” BD Yang, executive vice president of Samsung’s core component technology team, told The Verge, emphasizing Samsung’s work to manage silicon reactivity, swelling, and long-term cell stability, rather than prioritizing energy density alone. He called the Fold 8’s battery an “end-to-end improvement” over previous generations, combining higher capacity with “dependable performance.” [Image: The dual rear camera is an obvious downgrade from the Z Fold 7. Less encouraging are the cameras. Unlike Samsung’s previous Fold models, the Fold 8 is limited to two rear cameras, with no telephoto to be found. Both the main and ultrawide lenses use 50-megapixel sensors, which looks like an upgrade for the ultrawide, but means the main lens might be worse than the Z Fold 7’s 200-megapixel shooter — though we won’t know for sure until Samsung shares detailed specs like the sensor size and aperture and I get the chance to put the cameras to a more thorough test in my review. Still, Samsung’s foldable cameras already lagged behind its best slab phones, and the Fold 8 only appears to make matters worse. It’s also fallen behind the foldable competition in a few key ways. All three of Samsung’s new foldables remain limited to IP48, meaning they lack the comprehensive dust protection of Google’s Pixel 10 Pro Fold. And while Samsung says it’s overhauled the hinge and display stack with a new titanium-alloy film and a titanium plate below it, the changes aren’t enough to make the display crease anywhere near as subtle as on Oppo’s Find N6. Better are new magnets, which make the phone easier to open one-handed, and help it close with a satisfying click — though Samsung is still stubbornly refusing to integrate the internal magnets required for full Qi2 charging support. I won’t really know whether the Fold 8’s form factor is for me until I’ve spent more time with the phone, but after an hour or so, I’m surprisingly sold. I’ve never figured out a way to replace my work laptop with a foldable phone, but I could easily see one supplanting my tablet, which has been mostly relegated to a portable screen for in-flight entertainment. And with a bigger battery to boot, the Z Fold 8 might just last ’til I land. Still: $1,900 is an awful lot for any phone, and especially one that’s suffered such an obvious camera downgrade. It feels like even more considering this is an almost untested design, a new format that could be the future of foldables (especially if Apple has anything to say about it), but might arrive to the muted response that greeted last year’s Galaxy S25 Edge. An hour isn’t enough to know for certain either way, but after trying the Z Fold 8 in person, I’m already a fan.

articles.title: Preorders for Samsung’s new Z Fold and Flip 8 come with up to $350 in gift cards
articles.summary: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, and Galaxy Z Flip 8 are now available to preorder. Here’s how to buy them, and how to score the best deals.
articles.body: Samsung’s newest foldables are here. At Galaxy Unpacked, the company announced the Galaxy Z Flip 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8, and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. All three devices will be available on August 7th, but you can preorder them now starting at $1,199.99, $1,899.99, and $2,099.99, respectively. You probably noticed that Samsung’s foldable lineup looks a little different this year. Rather than simply updating the Galaxy Z Fold 7, Samsung now has two book-style foldables: the productivity-focused Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and the shorter, wider (when folded) Galaxy Z Fold 8 that’s geared more toward entertainment. The Galaxy Z Flip 8, meanwhile, is a touch thinner and lighter than its predecessor, but otherwise retains the same design as the Flip 7. All three phones also feature Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor and ship with Android 17 and One UI 9, which add new AI features like Gemini Intelligence task automation and Now Nudge, which proactively surfaces helpful suggestions like an event to your calendar. We’re still in the process of testing all three foldables, but after spending a few hours with them, we’ve shared our early hands-on impressions of the Galaxy Z Flip 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8, and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. Below, we’ve gathered everything you need to know about preordering Samsung’s new foldables, including pricing, carrier deals, and more. Where to preorder the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra starts at $2,099.99 when you buy the base model with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. If you want 512GB of storage, it costs $2,299.99, while 1TB of storage will set you back $2,699.99. The phone is available in violet shadow, graphite, cream, and shadow green, with the latter exclusive to Samsung’s online store. In terms of deals, Amazon is including a $350 gift card with preorders of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, while Best Buy is offering a $200 gift card. Samsung, meanwhile, is throwing in $200 in Samsung credit, plus the $30 reservation credit for those who reserved, and you can also save $100 with code PAYPAL100. The company’s additionally offering up to $100 off on select Samsung products. If you’re after Samsung’s most capable foldable, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is the one to preorder. It retains the design of the Z Fold 7 while adding a larger 5,000mAh silicon-carbon battery, plus faster 45W wired and 20W wireless charging. It offers up to 16GB of RAM and an upgraded camera system with a new 50-megapixel ultrawide sensor alongside its 200-megapixel main camera. Like the smaller Galaxy Z Fold 8, it also features Samsung’s new Flex Titanium display technology, which makes the crease far less noticeable. [Product: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra (256GB storage, 12GB RAM) | Where to preorder the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 starts at $1,899 for the base model with 256GB of storage and 12GB of RAM. You can also upgrade to 512GB of storage for $2,099.99 or 1TB of storage for $2,499.99. It’s available in lavender, graphite, cream, and a Samsung-online exclusive pistachio shade. If you’re looking to save some money, Amazon is offering a $350 gift card when you preorder the Galaxy Z Fold 8, while Best Buy includes a $200 gift card. If you buy directly from Samsung, you’ll receive $200 in Samsung credit, along with the $30 reservation credit if you reserved ahead of time, and can save $100 with code PAYPAL100. Samsung will also take up to $100 off select Samsung products. Unlike the larger, productivity-focused Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, the Z Fold 8 is designed more for entertainment, with a wider, shorter design that feels more like a small tablet when unfolded. The 4:3 inner display is better suited for reading and gaming than previous Fold models. It also shares many of the Ultra’s core features, including Samsung’s new Flex Titanium display technology so the crease is less noticeable, a bright 120Hz OLED display, and the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor. Samsung has also upgraded the Fold 7’s 4,400mAh battery to a larger 4,800mAh silicon-carbon cell, though it drops the telephoto lens found on both the Fold 7 and Fold 8 Ultra in favor of a dual-camera system. [Product: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 (256GB storage,12GB RAM) | Where to preorder the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 Samsung’s Galaxy Z Flip 8 starts at $1,199.99 for the phone with 256GB of storage and 12GB of RAM, while the 512GB model costs $1,399.99. It’s available in pink, graphite, cream, or mint colorways, with the latter exclusive to Samsung’s online store. If you preorder the Galaxy Z Flip 8 from Amazon, you’ll receive a $200 gift card, while Best Buy is including a $200 gift card as well. Samsung is offering $150 in Samsung credit, along with the $30 reservation credit if you reserved ahead of time for eligible customers. You also get up to $100 off on select Samsung products. Like its predecessor, the Galaxy Z Flip 8 features a clamshell design with a 6.9-inch OLED main display and a 4.1-inch OLED cover screen that lets you check notifications, reply to messages, and access apps without unfolding the phone. It also retains a 50-megapixel main camera paired with a 12-megapixel ultrawide and a 4,300mAh battery. The biggest changes are that it’s thinner and lighter, and now runs on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor. Samsung has also made the cover screen much more capable. You can now access notifications, quick settings, and a full app drawer with simple swipe gestures. You also no longer need Samsung’s Good Lock app to launch apps from the outer display. [Product: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 (256GB storage,12GB RAM) | Carrier offers and promotions * T-Mobile is offering new and existing customers the Galaxy Z Fold 8 for free when you trade in an eligible device on an Experience Beyond or Go5G Next plan, while the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is available for $200 with the same qualifying trade-in and plan. The carrier is also offering the Galaxy Z Flip 8 for $100 when you add a new line or trade in an eligible device on an eligible Experience More, Experience Beyond, Go5G Plus, or Go5G Next plan. * Verizon is taking up to $900 off the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, or Galaxy Z Flip 8 with an eligible phone trade-in on the Unlimited Ultimate or Unlimited Plus plans. Meanwhile, customers on the Unlimited Welcome plan can save up to $360. All discounts are applied as 36 monthly bill credits. * AT&T is offering up to $1,900 off the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra applied as monthly credits when you trade in an eligible phone on a Premium or higher-end plan. You can also get up to $1,000 off the Galaxy Z Fold 8 or Galaxy Z Flip 8 with an eligible trade-in on qualifying plans. AT&T is also bundling the Galaxy Watch 9 and Galaxy Tab A11 5G for $1.99 per month each with Galaxy Z Fold 8 purchases. Update, July 22nd: Added information about Verizon and AT&T’s deals.

articles.title: How the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Flip 8 phones compare
articles.summary: Samsung has announced the new Z Flip 8, Z Fold 8, and Z Fold 8 Ultra, and we have all the details about the specifications in one convenient table.
articles.body: Samsung’s latest round of folding Galaxy Z phones and updated smartwatches were announced at its July 2026 Unpacked event and are set to launch on August 7th. The Galaxy Z Flip 8, Fold 8, and Fold 8 Ultra don’t seem geared toward people who bought last year’s model; aside from a few design updates and AI features, there’s not a whole lot that’s new — unless we’re talking about the Z Fold 8. The Z Fold 8 is the foldable that will probably get the most attention in the US this year, that is, unless Apple’s rumored foldable arrives in the coming months. While its name makes it sound like the successor to last year’s Z Fold 7, it’s a new, shorter variation that starts at $1,899.99. It has a 7.6-inch main screen and a 5.5-inch exterior screen — noticeably smaller than the new $2,099.99 Z Fold 8 Ultra. It’s nearly as feature-packed as the Ultra, with some exceptions, like having a 50-megapixel main camera instead of a 200-megapixel lens, and a slightly smaller 4,800mAh battery. There are three configurations, with the 256GB and 512GB models sporting 12GB of memory and the 1TB model upgraded to 16GB of RAM. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is, in a lot of ways, a direct follow-up to the Z Fold 7, but with a new name. It has a 8-inch main screen and a 6.5-inch cover screen that are the same size and resolution as the previous model, along with the aforementioned 200-megapixel camera with 3x telephoto optical zoom. It has the same storage and memory configurations of the smaller Fold 8. Lastly, the Galaxy Z Flip 8 is the most affordable model, starting at $1,199.99. Of the three foldables, the Flip 8 seems to have the fewest hardware updates. Its battery capacity is unchanged, as are its camera specs. However, it has the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 instead of the Exynos 2500 used in the Flip 7. We’ll have to wait until the review to see if that change will bring improvements; our review of last year’s flip phone didn’t highlight performance issues with the Samsung-made chip. While that covers some of the surface-level changes, we have the full spec sheets below for your perusal. [Table: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 vs. Z Fold 8 vs. Z Fold 8 Ultra]

articles.title: I bought DJI’s banned camera — it was cheap and easy
articles.summary: The DJI Osmo Pocket 4 and Pocket 4P are banned in the United States, but that isn’t stopping smugglers.
articles.body: As a kid, I always imagined the “black market” would be like the movies: Shady vendors hawking illicit goods along dusty streets. But if you want a banned DJI Osmo Pocket 4 or Pocket 4 Pro camera in the US, you can just reach for your phone. They’re on Temu, AliExpress, eBay, Mercari — even Amazon and Newegg — with fast, free shipping and no risk of tariffs or seizures. That’s because these cameras are already inside the United States, despite rules that ban them from entering the country. This past month, I ordered a DJI Osmo Pocket 4 Pro from Temu. It arrived just four days later, shipped directly from a fulfillment center in Oregon, where a cross-border logistics company called Blue Ocean stuffed it into a FedEx baggie for me. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: After all the Temu discounts, I spent only $659.28 for the Pocket 4P Vlog Combo with the Mic Mini 2 and FrameTap remote control that my colleague Dom Preston tested for us. That’s less than I paid for the Osmo Pocket 3 combo back in 2023. [Image: For me, it was worth putting up with Temu’s casino-like experience. YMMV. These cameras are banned from import into the United States, The Verge can confirm. While public records show that both DJI cameras did clear the FCC in advance of the December 2025 future foreign drone ban, both were certified within 30 days of that ban — which let the FCC use a little-known power in December to easily take those certifications away. The FCC repeatedly refused to provide an on-the-record statement about how it used that rule, 47 CFR 2.962(f), to get rid of the certification. But when we asked DJI about it, the company confirmed to The Verge that its new cameras are banned. Without FCC certification, no device with a radio can be imported, marketed, or sold in the United States. The FCC’s ban doesn’t take away your existing drones or cameras, but it’s supposed to block new ones from coming in — but once again, it appears the FCC doesn’t have the manpower or focus to actually ground them. DJI claims it’s not involved in the US sales we’re seeing. A company spokesperson, responding anonymously from DJI’s press email address and who did not provide a name when we asked, shared this company statement: > DJI was informed of the FCC’s determination and has fully complied with it. Osmo Pocket 4P and Osmo Pocket 4 were not released in the United States when the products were launched globally. DJI does not offer or sell these products through its official U.S. channels and did not distribute these products in the U.S. market. Any products that may be offered by independent third-party sellers are not products sold or distributed by DJI in the U.S. DJI has no involvement in those third-party sales. After inspecting my own DJI Pocket 4 Pro from Temu, I think it’s at least plausible that third-party sellers are acting on their own. The camera starts up with Chinese menus, for example, and neither the camera’s regulatory screen nor the box display an FCC ID, so DJI probably didn’t just say “screw it, ship the US version anyhow.” [Image: The packaging is primarily in English, Chinese, and French, but has regulatory markings from many countries including Canada, China, Brazil, Japan, Korea, and the UAE. [Image: The box does include the “This device complies with part 15 of the FCC Rules” boilerplate. But there’s been a pattern of funny behavior with DJI, whose technology has regularly been popping up in gadgets repackaged by companies like Xtra, which ships near-identical cameras in the US. While neither DJI nor Xtra have confirmed or denied a relationship to The Verge, Xtra is now facing a US ban, too. If you’re wondering why cameras are getting caught up in a drone ban, you’re not alone. I find it hard to believe that an almost-entirely-offline camera poses a national security threat to the United States like the Trump administration claims. But we do know how they’re getting caught in the ban. When the US government banned future foreign drones last December, it also announced it was incorporating a ban on “communications or video surveillance equipment” from DJI and Autel Robotics. The game of whack-a-drone continues elsewhere. This week, HoverAir, aka Zero Zero Robotics, announced that it had secured FCC certification for its new Versa drone, which transforms from a DJI Pocket-like camera into a flying camera by adding a pair of propeller wings. Public records show it did so by claiming its camera isn’t on the Covered List, which is true — only DJI, Autel, Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hikvision, and Dahua are part of the camera ban. But all new foreign drones are automatically on the Covered List unless they get a waiver. Does giving a camera wings actually dodge the drone ban? You can read my take on that here.

articles.title: My big, fat, technophobic cat
articles.summary: A tale of trying to get a rotund and sassy cat to lose weight using automated feeders, water fountains, poop robots and toys.
articles.body: My cat Pablo is a voluptuous boy. His primordial pouch, originally thought to protect cats’ squishy insides, hangs low and wobbles to and fro. Once, when he was five or six, a vet sternly sat my spouse and me down, gravely stating, “He’s simply too young to be this fat.” Pablo didn’t care, but we were traumatized. Now that he’s 10, the vets have repeatedly scolded us. All 20 pounds of his rotundity, they say, cannot continue. The specter of diabetes and kidney problems, and the fact that his obesity combined with a too-small pee-pee hole increases his risk of urinary crystals, mean that a diet is urgent. I hear this every year. I keep saying “We are trying!!” The vets say, “Try harder! There are plenty of gadgets and toys you can use to stimulate enrichment, manage food, and encourage exercise!” What I don’t think the vets understand is that the state of pet tech is simply no match for Pablo. As with humans, the key to weight loss in cats is a strict calorie deficit and increased activity. The problem is diets can be notoriously difficult for felines. Their small bodies don’t require that much food, spaying or neutering alters cat metabolisms, and they are famously finicky creatures. They’re also reliant on routines and, in Pablo’s case, can be heavily resistant to change. [Image: His Royal Rotundity really is a sweet boy when I’m not making him pose for photos. Pablo’s war on pet tech and diets all started with a Litter-Robot 4. We initially got it because Pablo’s poops were olfactory crimes. Manually scooping them was causing marital strife. (“He’s YOUR cat,” is what I’d say early on in our relationship. “He’s OUR cat,” my spouse retorted once we got married.) Meanwhile, lifting Pablo onto one of our scales to monitor his weight would earn many yowls and skippity paps to the face. The Litter-Robot seemed like a clever solution because (1) automated scooping and (2) there’s a built-in scale. Whenever he does his business, I can log into the companion app to see how much he weighs (as well as monitor his bowel movements). For a time, Pablo allowed us our folly. He was not a fan of the Litter-Robot. He eyed the spinning, globe-shaped bonnet with suspicion, but as a sophisticated, fancy boy, he wasn’t prone to pooping just anywhere. But then we moved to a four-story row home. My spouse and I viewed the three flights of stairs as a good chance for us, Pablo, and our other cat, Petey, to get in more steps. Three of us agreed. You can guess which one of us did not. For logistical and cleaning purposes, we were not schlepping the Litter-Robot 4 up beyond the second floor. The thing weighs 24 pounds empty, and the thought of repeatedly carrying that up and down three flights of stairs to hose it down was too much. (It’s already bad enough that any litter box on an upper floor requires regularly carrying 15- to 30-pound bags of fresh litter up and down multiple flights.) In our previous apartments, we’d always put the Litter Robot, automated feeders, and pet fountains near the kitchen. But cats are territorial creatures. Before moving, Pablo and Petey shared spaces and litter boxes begrudgingly. With more space, they each established their own kingdoms. Pablo claimed the top floor — the bedroom. Petey claimed the second, where the Litter-Robot and the comfy couch reside. With the resulting borders settled into law, Pablo promptly stopped using the Litter-Robot. He also refuses to venture downstairs, except at 10PM each night to yell and enforce bedtime. We tried to encourage him to use the expensive poop robot anyway. In protest, he began shitting on the carpet right outside my third-floor office door. The turd war continued for three weeks before we caved. I’m not rich enough to buy a second Litter-Robot. The newest model costs $800, and while I enjoy a workout, the Litter-Robot 5 is even heavier at 28.7 pounds empty. So I bought a $20 stainless steel, not-very-smart litter box — and a smart pet scale designed to go under it. To save our noses, we put the litter box into one of those stealthy litter box enclosures that look like a regular credenza. Pablo did not appreciate the new setup. At first, I thought he objected to his new pellet litter. We switched to an ultrafine microcrystal litter for his sensitive paws. He continued shitting outside my office. Turns out, he didn’t like that the under-box scale made the litter box enclosure feel cramped. We removed it, and now I’m back to weighing him manually every few weeks. Pablo 2, Tech 0. [Image: [Image: Pablo doesn’t enjoy any form of movement that doesn’t end in a cuddle or treat. Ball tracks? Not a fan. The extremely cute Enabot robot? Icily ignored. We tried robot vacuums so he’d be forced to at least move rooms. Eventually, he started sitting on tables and chairs, watching disdainfully as the robovacs jammed themselves into furniture. Wand toys are viewed with snooty disgust. After a few half-hearted swats, he flops on his back and declares playtime over. He took one look at a cat tower and went, “Nah.” Pablo’s primary amusements are his catnip squirrel, pancaking his emotional support Squishmallows, and sometimes, if the mood strikes him, chasing a laser for three minutes. All he really wants is for me and my spouse to sit quietly with him on the bed, give him chin scratches, obey his strict sleeping schedule, and feed him on time. Case in point, I sometimes test smart alarm clocks. But as I wrote in my review of the now-defunct Amazon Halo Rise, Pablo is an “affection eater.” This may seem absurd to non-cat owners, but some cats genuinely insist on company at mealtime. Pablo requires a witness, someone to sit on the floor next to him as he painstakingly eats each kibble bit one by one. (And to guard his meal from Petey.) He insists breakfast is promptly at 5:30AM, so when the automatic feeder goes off, I must sit with him for 10 to 15 minutes as he eats, occasionally redirecting Petey’s greedy face to his own bowl. He obviously doesn’t like any gadget that may encourage a variable wake-up time, such as a smart alarm clock that gently glows depending on sunrise times. He has knocked plenty off the nightstand, viewing his method of smothering me with his fluffy belly as superior. After viewing some TikToks of cats enjoying walking pads, I called in a smart walking pad for review. Healthy for me, potentially healthy for my cats to get more steps in. Alas, this too ended up being a bust. I got stressed out by the smart features. Even the more mischievous Petey, with his one brain cell, could not process the concept of himself walking on the pad. All he did was bat at my feet while I walked on it. Pablo rolled off the belt when I tried putting him on it at a very low speed. Pablo 6, Tech 0. [Image: [Image: In case you were wondering, Pablo also doesn’t consent to the pet surveillance state. He’s a handsome boy, but he hates getting his photo taken. Every single photo taken for this piece required bribes and cajoling. Most of the photos I have of him on my camera roll are of him sleeping, belly up. He’s learned to turn his head away from smartphone cameras. Petey now also does the same. So much so that my main use for smart glasses cameras is to get cute cat videos. (They have not yet learned what a white recording light is.) I installed various pet cams because I was curious about how often Pablo was actually eating and moving around. I can also be a helicopter pet mom whenever we travel. But whereas Petey will purposefully mog for the pet cam, rolling around on the living room floor at 3AM like a demonic potato, Pablo will slink off into closets outside the camera’s field of view. I thought we outsmarted him by buying a fancy Petlibro automatic feeder with a built-in camera before a two-week vacation to Italy. Nope. We’d only just landed in Rome when, after checking in on the feed, we saw that the feeder had been knocked over. I had to immediately call my pet sitter to go and cater to his whims. Pablo 7, Tech 1 (I count the smart glasses as a win) After eight years of technological warfare, however, there are two gadgets that Pablo tolerates — likes, even. One is the Petlibro cat fountain. He loves a fountain. The other is our Eight Sleep smart mattress cover. Like all cats, he loves a warm surface. So now, instead of climbing into a toasty bed every night, I have a staring contest with Pablo as he dares me to move him from my spot. I always win because I can just shove him over. But it’s not without some irritated meows and a lot of sass. [Image: Pablo hates tech. (We also do not leave any uneaten food after supervised mealtime. That’s how he got so chonky to begin with.) Pablo 7, Tech 3. As for Pablo’s weight loss plan… The next obvious step would be RFID feeders to be 100 percent sure that Petey and Pablo aren’t overeating when we can’t supervise meals. You stick a collar with an RFID tag so that the feeder only allows a specific cat to eat. The only problem is they’re expensive, our current feeders aren’t broken, and Pablo hates collars. I have debated sticking a pet fitness tracker on Pablo. Ultimately, I decided against it because not only does he hate collars, but I already attempted it with my elderly Yorkie before she passed. The data tends to be more wellness-focused than actually useful for encouraging exercise. Frankly, we adopted Petey because we thought a younger cat might encourage him to move around and play. Petey adores Pablo. The affection remains unrequited. My spouse has given up. Pablo is just destined to be round, they say. They constantly remind me that we already strictly control his food intake, and the pounds ain’t coming off. I happen to think that maybe this is a Petey-and-tech problem. Perhaps a third kitten might do the trick.

articles.title: Garmin’s new Fenix 9 adds brighter screens and smoother map panning
articles.summary: Garmin just launched its Fenix 9 and 9 Pro smartwatches, both of which come with brighter OLED displays. The Fenix 9 Pro model also offers satellite connectivity across all three size options.
articles.body: Garmin just took the wraps off its new line of rugged Fenix 9 smartwatches, with the base model featuring an OLED display with a brightness of up to 3,000 nits, making it twice as bright as its predecessor. Starting at $999.99 for the 43mm case option, the Fenix 9 has 50 percent more RAM and an upgraded map engine, allowing for faster panning. It also comes with a scratch-resistant sapphire lens, an increased 64GB of storage, and a bunch of new software-based features, like Garmin Epic. This feature groups all the workouts you’ve done over several days, weeks, or months to create an “Epic” that shows your health and performance data within that period. There are also new stamina tracking metrics and expanded rucking features that let you change the weight of your pack during a workout. Garmin says the Fenix 9 offers up to 29 days of battery life in smartwatch mode on the largest 51mm size. [Image: [Image: [Image: The Fenix 9 Pro starts at $1,099.99 and expands on these upgrades with a new titanium case. It has InReach satellite or LTE connectivity available on all three 43mm, 47mm, and 51mm options for an extra $100 and a $7.99 / month subscription. The largest Fenix 9 Pro variation also offers a 1.5-inch OLED display for the first time. That’s just a little bigger than the 1.3-inch and 1.4-inch displays available with the smaller case sizes across the Fenix 9 lineup. [Image: [Image: [Image: Additionally, the 47mm and 51mm Fenix 9 Pro models offer a solar-charged display option that promises up to 57 days of battery life (with the caveat that you spend three hours per day outside in 50,000 lux conditions).  The Fenix 9 lineup is available in an array of case and band color combinations. The new devices will be available to order starting August 28th.

articles.title: How Modern Appointment Viewing Shows Are Bringing Back ‘Watercooler’ Television
articles.summary: There’s nothing better than sitting on the couch to binge your favorite TV show. Or, maybe, there is. In the era of streaming, binge-watching is easier than...
articles.body:
There's nothing better than sitting on the couch to binge your favorite TV show. Or, maybe, there is. In the era of streaming, binge-watching is easier than ever. So, it seems potentially incongruous that appointment viewing — watching a television show when it first airs — is so capable of seizing the collective attention of viewers.

But fandom is a powerful force, and appointment viewing has tamed the beast into something fearsome. Rather than encouraging viewers to settle in with episode after episode queued up, shows like "Survivor," "The Pitt" and summer's guilty pleasure "Love Island" make their fans wait for it.

How 'The Pitt' Production Designer Expanded the Emergency Room for Season 2

'Survivor' vs. 'The Traitors': Will Emmy Voters Finally Give the Original Reality Juggernaut Its Due?

'The Pitt' Season 3 Trailer: Dr. Robby's First Day Back Is Filled With More Medical Emergencies

It's not a new concept; "Survivor" has been rocking weekly episode drops since its first foray in 2000 on the Bornean beaches. But it has reached a new fervor with watch parties popping up across the country and "Love Island'"s reality flair convincing millions to watch almost daily as hot singles couple up.

There's obvious incentive to watch when an episode airs if everyone is talking about it; you can hardly open your phone during "Love Island" season without seeing a spoiler. And the reality dating show takes it a step further: Fans can vote live on who must leave the villa and who lives to flirt another day.

"Survivor" has dabbled in the fan vote mechanism, too. An extra prize in "Survivor: All-Stars," casting selection for "Survivor: Cambodia — Second Chance" and gameplay elements in "Survivor 50: In the Hands of the Fans" were all left, well, in the hands of the fans.

Even a non-reality show like "The Pitt" has capitalized on the power behind scheduled releases. The first two episodes of Season 1 dropped concurrently on Jan. 9, 2025, but every subsequent episode has been released on a weekly schedule.

As with any show that received such critical esteem as the Pittsburgh-based medical drama, whose first season won five of its 13 Emmy nominations, Season 2 was accused online of a sophomore slump. Those critical social media fans were accused right back of not watching as intended (i.e., bandwagon binge-ing Season 1 and being upset about starting Season 2 before that was possible).

"Survivor" showrunner and Emmy-nominated host Jeff Probst describes the difference between binge-watching and appointment viewing as the difference between a flight and a road trip. Both get you to the destination, but with one, the time spent is part of the experience.

Viewers had a week to reckon with the knowledge that there was an active shooter event in the first season of "The Pitt" before the fallout reached the Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center in the next episode. Skipping a night of "Love Island" this summer might have meant a fan's favorite couple exiting the villa — and certainly meant not understanding the social media memes and reactions the next day. Sure, you can binge old seasons of "Survivor," but you lose the emotional experience of living with Probst snuffing the torch of a beloved player.

The time between episodes is where fandom finds its home: reacting, interacting and generally causing a stir around a show in a way that binge-watches can't always pull off. "The Pitt" has been lauded as a return to classic television, the kind of "water cooler" show that inspires next-day conversations with coworkers.

"That waiting period creates a different kind of emotional investment because the audience begins supplying part of the experience," Probst says. Binge-watching builds momentum, but appointment viewing makes fans sit with the emotion.

Physical water coolers may be no more, but modern appointment viewing shows are fighting the impatience of binge watchers, and they're winning.

articles.title: Dolly Parton Was a ‘Proud’ Producer Behind “Buffy the Vampire Slayer”: ‘That Little Show Did Great’
articles.summary: “I was very excited about the show. That little show did great,” the country music legend said of the beloved series, on which she was an executive producer
articles.body:
Dolly Parton died at age 80 on Tuesday, Aug. 25

One of the many projects the singer was involved in during her career was the hit series Buffy the Vampire Slayer, on which she is credited as an executive producer

"That little show did great," Parton once said

Dolly Parton played a role in one of the biggest TV hits of the late '90s.

The country music legend, who died at age 80 on Aug. 25 , was at one point "very involved" behind the scenes of Buffy the Vampire Slayer , the Sarah Michelle Gellar –led series that ran for seven seasons from 1997 to 2003.

"A lot of my work was done just conversing back and forth with the business people there. And I'd go out for meetings now and then," Parton told Business Insider in 2024. She is listed as an executive producer on the series but told the outlet, "I have to give more people credit on Buffy the Vampire Slayer than me. A lot of people did so much work on that."

"I was very excited about the show. That little show did great," Parton said.

She added that "didn't get to meet all of" the cast, "but I wanted them to know that I was there for them, I was proud of them, and they were doing a great job."

Gellar, 49, previously spoke about Parton's involvement in the series, calling it a "little-known fact" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in 2023.

"The legend Dolly Parton was a producer," Gellar said. "We never saw her [but] we'd get Christmas gifts in the beginning that would have our name, and I would think, 'She doesn't even know who I am.' And then one day, someone asked her about it, and she complimented the show and my performance. I was like, 'Oh, I can die now. Dolly Parton knows who I am and thinks I'm good.'"

After news of Parton's death, Gellar wrote on Instagram, "Just being a small part of the great history of @dollyparton is everything to me," and shared a clip of the singer talking about Buffy on Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen in 2021.

In that clip, Parton explained that her production company with former manager Sandy Gallin, Sandollar Productions, helped with Buffy . "We were a small part of that. I was very, very proud to be part of that," she told host Cohen at the time.

The news of Parton's death was announced in a video by her nephew Bryan Seaver. "I'm representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next. This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven't truly felt it until now. It is an honor, an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness."

"My family and I have shared a lifetime of beautiful memories with Dolly, but so have you. She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family whether you liked it or not. Our family and the team she has entrusted with her legacy will work diligently to ensure her spirit will live with us forever. Dolly was a farmer, just like her daddy; he farmed the soil, she farmed songs and happiness. Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life of wearing heavy rhinestones, she finally deserves to be comfortable and have some rest," her nephew continued.

"Rest in peace, Aunt Dolly — Aunt, Granny, Gigi. May God bless Dolly Parton, and may God bless you all. She will always love you."

The legendary singer's death came four days after she told PEOPLE she was "dealing with some health issues that I just didn't pay attention to when I was watching over Carl ," referring to her late husband, Carl Dean , who died in 2025.

"Even though I'm still healin', I'm still workin'! You know me — as I've often said — I've dreamed myself into a corner and I still have so many things I want to achieve, so I'm gonna keep on working as long as I can to see everything come to life," she said.

articles.title: Why the Projection for the Houston Rockets to Earn the 3rd Seed in the West is Realistic
articles.summary: The projection of Houston finishing with a 51-31 record is achievable for a few reasons.
articles.body:
On August 24, 2026, ESPN revealed its projected standings for the upcoming 2026-27. ESPN projected the Houston Rockets to finish as the third seed, tied with the Denver Nuggets . Both teams would finish with a 51-31 record.

Considering that the Rockets finished the last two seasons with a 52-30 record, these projections are reasonable. Along with Houston's recent roster additions, the development of the young core, and the return of injured players, the third seed seems achievable if not likely.

Houston signed Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanović from free agency this summer, adding much-needed roster depth and veteran leadership. Smart's strong and motivating locker-room presence, ball-handling and playmaking skills, and elite perimeter defense will improve the second unit. Bogdanović's signing adds a three-point threat to the team, which the Rockets lacked last season.Houston has a very strong young core.

Amen Thompson has developed into one of the best young two-way players in the NBA. Thompson's length and speed make him one of the most versatile perimeter defenders. He also has a strong interior presence. Out of his average of 18.3 points per game, 12.1 of those points came directly in the paint. His athleticism and creativity make him an elite finisher in the paint, which is proven by his 70.5% field goal percentage in the restricted area.

Amen Thompson's weakness is his three-point and mid-range shooting, in which he averaged an abysmal 21.6% and 27.8%, respectively. However, Houston hired Chip Engelland to improve the team's shooting. Engelland's track record shows that he can work his magic and make Thompson a respectable shooter.

Engelland will also focus on improving the 24-year-old Alperen Şengün. Şengün shot a poor 30.5% from deep and 35.5% from mid-range. On top of this, he also averages 69.1% from the free-throw line.

If Engelland can improve their shooting, it will force the opposing teams to spread out to the perimeter, thereby creating space in the paint and widening the cutting lanes.

Houston's roster will also be bolstered by the addition of both Steven Adams and Fred VanVleet . VanVleet missed the entire 2025-26 season due to an ACL tear, but is now healthy and increasingly motivated for the upcoming season. Adams suffered a severe ankle sprain in January, missing the rest of the season.

These improvements to the Rockets' roster should be enough to land them in the top five of the Western Conference. Pinnacle has the over/under for Houston's total season wins at 47.5, meaning that the team will have to perform only slightly above the sharp predictions to earn the third seed and win 51 games.

The indication is that although the prediction is not probable, it is certainly realistic. Will the improvements in the roster and management be enough?

articles.title: ‘AGT’ Recap: Who Got Mel B.’s Live Golden Buzzer?
articles.summary: Night two of the Live Shows featured 11 more acts hitting the stage for a shot at the Semifinals.
articles.body:
The Quarterfinals continued on the August 25 episode of America's Got Talent . Eleven more acts took the stage in hopes of moving on in the competition.

Like last week, there was one Live Golden Buzzer in play. After Howie Mandel gave his to Hundred Fingers on August 18, sending them straight to the Finals, the power was in Mel B. 's hands this time around. America will vote for their favorites of the rest of the contestants, and three of those acts will move onto the Semifinals during tomorrow night's results show.

Because Simon Cowell is away from the show for a few weeks due to a "routine" procedure relating to his back injury , his seat was left empty, leaving Mandel, Mel, and Sofia Vergara to offer commentary from the judges' table.

Scroll down for a recap of the night's performances and to find out who got the Golden Buzzer.

Kicking off the night was LaRussell with a rap performance, accompanied by his friends from the Bay Area.

"First of all, I love what you guys stand for. I can feel the energy literally bouncing off the stage," Mel B. said. "I did find it a little bit chaotic. There was a lot going on. But like I said, your energy was right up there. It was. And that's the part that I enjoyed. I almost wish you had a few more days to rehearse it. I felt like you were a little bit out of breath, but I could feel the excitement."

The audience boo-ed Mel's response, but Vergara jumped in to say, "I do think this was a step up from the audition. I love it. I think it's amazing what they do." Finally, Mandel added, "I think it was good, I think it was entertaining. I don't know if it's at the level Season 21 is looking for. It felt like a musical recital from a high school to me."

The second performance was from aerialist Veronika Goroshkova, who was one of Vergara's Golden Buzzers during the Auditions. She did another wild routine, this time set to Taylor Swift 's "The Fate of Ophelia."

"Now you know why I gave her the Golden Buzzer. There is no one like her," Vergara raved. "The fascinating thing about me for you is you make it seem so easy, so effortless."

Mandel called Veronika "amazing" and said no other aerialist on the show has been as "graceful" as her. Mel B. added, "What else can I say? Everybody's said everything. You were that powerful, the sponge of my microphone popped off. Graceful. Just brilliant."

Just days after celebrating her 18th birthday, Bety hit the stage for a performance of TK TK. Bety was one of Mel B.'s callback acts who made the Quarterfinals after her second chance performance, and now her fate is in America's hands.

Bety sang Sam Smith's "Fire on Fire" for the Live Show. "You know I'm a massive fan of yours. Your voice is like velvet," Mel said. "I do think you played it a little bit too safe tonight. I know your vocal range is so wide, but it was beautiful."

Vergara told Bety she already looks like a "big star" on stage. "You wanted to do this your whole life and it shows in your performance. I love it," she gushed. Meanwhile, Mandel said Bety is "one of the best singers" on the season, but admitted, "That song doesn't have a ton of range. You have a ton of range. I love your audition so much more than this."

Come Here, a dance group, took the stage next. Heading into the big night, the group dealt with some setbacks as their choreographer had a prior commitment and couldn't make it to L.A. until just 12 hours before showtime.

The routine got a standing ovation from all three judges. "What a unique blend of contemporary and ballet, very original choreography," Mandel said. "You're amazing, you deserve to be here."

Vergara added, "Breathtaking. It was amazing. It was perfection. No tricks, no flips, it's just a unit." Mel B. said she thought the routine was "absolutely incredible," and it even seemed like she was going to press the Golden Buzzer for a second after a brief side conversation with Mandel. However, she held off for a future performance.

Music duo Nyjah Music and Zyah Rhythm were one of Cowell's callback acts. They came to the Live Shows hoping to show a new level of confidence with a performance of "I Swear."

The judges cringed through the performance, and Mel B. even hit her red buzzer to signify that she was not impressed. "You guys can sing, you can harmonize," Mandel began. "I think Simon said it in the package and I think he's right … it takes experience and time. I think you're going to be great. I think you're going to do well. But I feel it's just about experience. The nerves are kind of showing."

Mel B. said, "I actually felt I did you a favor. I think you need a lot more time, a lot more experience, and at this point in the competition, this should be your best. I should be able to feel the hunger, the passion. It was just like you were taking a walk on Malibu beach without a care in the world. I didn't see it." She urged the guys to practice and come back with "more determination."

Vergara had to agree with Mel and Mandel that Nyjah and Zyah played it too safe and needed more experience. "I think you need to keep working and follow your dream because you guys are good," she concluded.

Magician Geno Ploeger was up next. After previously working with AGT winner Mat Franco, Geno is now ready to make a name for himself. Mandel warned him during his audition that he needed to do something more original, and he came ready to show that off.

"I don't even have words," Mel B. said afterwards. Vergara raved, "This was original. I'm so glad you paid attention to what Howie told you. This feels like you. It suits you. This is how you have to keep doing it."

Finally, Mandel gushed, "I said if you come back, you do you, something I have never seen. You. Did. You."

Cowell called Patrox "one of the most original acts we've ever seen" when he auditioned, and he showed off his unique backwards dance skills once again.

"I think it's so clever what you do. I don't really fully understand what the hell is happening, but it's fun," Vergara said. "To make something like that work on a stage like this is not easy."

Mel B. admitted she liked that Patrox is "so excited," but again, she said she didn't understand the concept of his dancing and backwards replay. Mandel jumped in to say, "I think what you do is incredibly unique. It's a trick. It's an amazing trick. I applaud you."

Teenage rocker Nene Royal took the stage next. After getting through to the Quarterfinals as one of Mandel's callback acts, she was ready to prove she belonged, especially since her audition went so viral.

Is she wearing a painted t-shirt with her own name on it? #AGT pic.twitter.com/Bx9hfM03iq — AGT Time Podcast (@agttimepod) August 26, 2026

Is she wearing a painted t-shirt with her own name on it? #AGT pic.twitter.com/Bx9hfM03iq

After Nene's performance of "Black Hole Sun" by Soundgarden, Mandel addressed NBC directly, saying, "Give her the $1 million. Right now!" Vergara said, "I think you can really win this competition. You can sing and play that guitar. No wonder everybody on the street asks me about you!"

Mel could barely get a word in edgewise over the loud screams of the audience. "You are just the most humblest, sweet, young lady, and then you come out on this stage and it's a different vibe," she applauded.

Vergara urged her to push the Golden Buzzer, and Mel B. said, "I love really good vocals. I'm a 90s girl. I'm into pop music. That kind of music is not my vibe. But your vocals are on point, your guitar is on point, your look, your energy, your vibe … how could I not do this?!" And with that, Nene is in the Finals!

Mackenzie Sol , one of Mel B.'s audition Golden Buzzers, returned to the stage next. He wanted to do something different for the Live Shows, so he sang Tate McRae's "You Broke Me First," and got emotional at the end of the performance.

"That was so good," Mel B. promised. "That was everything. The feelings, the trills, the vocals, the voice, the everything. That was just … yeah." Vergara told Mackenzie, "I think the girls are going to go crazy with you. So handsome, such a beautiful energy, such a beautiful voice. I loved your audition and I love you tonight."

Mandel said she hopes people vote for Mackenzie, and Mel jumped in to add, "I really, really, really hope people vote for you!" Mandel also made sure Mackenzie knew he "rose to the occasion" of having to perform after Nene.

Extreme danger act (and married couple) Brad and Tracy came with another death-defying routine next. Mel was so grossed out by Brad's sword-swallowing trick that she pushed her red buzzer and turned away.

The act did not quite resonate and fell very flat, although Mandel did give a standing ovation. "The energy and the showmanship … you cant even put into words what we just saw," he said. "It is so bad, it is amazing."

Vergara added, "I could not stop thinking about what your neighbors think about you two. You guys are scary. Tracy, you should be in a scary movie. You're perfect, your acting, your delivery. It's amazing. I don't know if this is good, if it's bad. We can't stop looking at you guys, so I guess it's a good thing."

Mel admitted that "this is a genre where people do things to themselves like that," but said, "I find it more comedic. I do like the vibe. But just … why?"

The final performance of the night was from singing duo Butter and Grit.

"Your vocals have got exponentially more than amazing. That song, and it's an original … I love your friendship, I love your vibe, America needs to vote for you," Mel B. gushed.

What Is 'AGT' Finalist Preacher Lawson Doing Now?

Vergara said she loved Butter and Grit's original songs. "They feel like they're already hits, that they've been hits. I really love your friendship and relationship," she added. Mandel concluded, "There's nothing more America than that type of music and the way you sing it."

articles.title: Samsung launches speedy P9 portable SSD.
articles.summary:
It uses a USB4 interface to reach speeds up to 4,000MB/s. Hitting those peak speeds requires a native USB4 or Thunderbolt 4/5 port, and dedicated Thunderbolt 5 SSDs can hit an even faster 6,000MB/s if you’re willing to pay. The P9 starts at $339.99 for 1TB, or $2,699.99 for a whopping 8TB. Sales start August 31st.
[Image: Samsung’s Portable P9-Series come in 1TB, 2TB, 4TB, and 8TB capacities. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Samsung-Semiconductors-P9-P7-SSD-USB4-Gamescom-2026_Main4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

articles.title: Karishma Tanna shares postpartum routine; reveals what she eats and drinks during this phase
articles.summary: New mom Karishma Tanna has shared a glimpse of her postpartum routine as she adjusts to motherhood. The actress opened up about the food, drinks and o.
articles.body: New mom Karishma Tanna has shared a glimpse of her postpartum routine as she adjusts to motherhood. The actress opened up about the food, drinks and other things that have been helping her during this phase.Taking to Instagram, Karishma shared that her days currently revolve around nourishing, healing and pumping. She also spoke about staying hydrated and caring for herself after childbirth.Sharing a series of pictures, the actress wrote, âSharing a little glimpse of my postpartum care routineâwhat I eat and drink to support my milk supply, how I care for sore nipples, ease my back pain and keep myself hydrated through the day. Lately, this is what my days look likeâ¦nourishing, healing, pumping and repeating.âShe further added, âAlso hot and cold compresses are also very very helpful and important And please wear the belly support belt everyday . I am wearing it too Details of everything in the caption. Let me know if these tips are helpful Mommies.âThe pictures showed Karishma with a cup of shatavari powder mixed with hot water, which she uses to support milk production. She also shared Hira bol edible gums for back pain, mukhwas for digestion and to help prevent gas, along with dried coconut and hydrating drinks. She also included saunf, jeera and ajwain water, a manual and an electric breast pump, and nipple cream as part of her postpartum routine.Earlier, Karishma had shared a throwback picture from a photoshoot taken when she was one month pregnant. Recalling that time, the actress revealed that she was quietly carrying what she described as âthe most beautiful secretâ while preparing for a new chapter in her life.For the unversed, Karishma Tanna and her husband, Varun Bangera, became parents to their first child, a baby boy, on July 29, 2026.

articles.title: Hearing tech startup Legato emerges from stealth with $12M and a peek at its AI hearing glasses | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The glasses, called Legato Frames, integrate the company’s patented hearing-assistance technology into the arms of eyewear frames.
articles.body:
Hearing loss affects an estimated 50 million adults in the United States, but only around 20% of those with diagnosed hearing loss seek treatment. Legato , a new hearing tech company, aims to close that gap.

The startup is emerging from stealth on Wednesday with $12 million in funding and a first look at its AI hearing glasses, the company told TechCrunch exclusively. The glasses, called Legato Frames, integrate the company’s patented hearing-assistance technology into the arms of eyewear frames. Legato Frames are expected to launch later this fall.

Legato was founded by Mehul Trivedi and Steve Romine, who bring extensive experience in wearables and hearing care from Bose, where Trivedi led the creation of Bose Frames and Romine ran the hearing aids division. Trivedi left Bose to work at EssilorLuxottica, where he led smart eyewear efforts and worked on the Meta Ray-Bans, while Romine went on to serve as COO of hearing care company Audicus.

After spending years at larger companies, Trivedi took some time off to explore the intersection of hearing technology and smart eyewear. During that time, Trivedi came across technology he believed could bring the two together, so he contacted Romine and the pair founded Legato in late 2024.

“Our goal is to make hearing as ubiquitous as vision,” Trivedi said in an interview with TechCrunch. “It’s kind of a no-brainer that you go to an eye exam, you get your glasses, you wear your glasses, and you’re happy, and you do that for the rest of your life — and the idea of it being blurry again where you would just stop wearing them is not a consideration. I think that’s what we want to do with hearing: just make it something that people address and almost forget about.”

Legato is targeting people with mild to moderate hearing loss, which represents the largest segment of the hearing-loss population, the startup says.

The company started with the goal of making hearing care more accessible by addressing the cost, comfort, and stigma associated with traditional hearing aids. Legato set out to make the glasses as small and lightweight as possible, and developed a proprietary acoustic system, signal-processing stack, and mechanical architecture to achieve it.

Traditional hearing aids often use directional microphones to focus on sounds coming from a particular direction, which works well in quiet settings but can be difficult in noisy environments, such as restaurants. Legato takes a different approach by using an AI-powered system to differentiate between background noise and voices, amplifying only the voices.

The goal is to make conversations clearer without creating the cognitively draining listening experience that can come with some traditional hearing aids.

“We wanted to deliver an experience that was unique,” Trivedi said. “So a form factor that’s really discreet and looks normal. They’re meant to feel and look like regular glasses. And so, we want it to be a product that’s effortless, easy to use, with kind of no controls that you need to fiddle with, works everywhere, works throughout your day, doesn’t need a ton of configuration, and just delivers you better hearing.”

While the frames have an open-ear design, sound isn’t broadcast to people around you. They feature a dual-speaker system that directs sound toward the wearer while canceling sound that escapes, reducing sound by 99% just a few inches away from the ear.

The company’s funding, which is from Neotribe Ventures, Listen, and Village Global, has largely gone toward product development, along with marketing efforts.

“We have an opportunity to address a population with this product and build something that delivers without all the compromises of traditional hearing aids,” Trivedi said. “Hearing, at first glance, it’s not so much just like ‘I want to hear the TV better.’ It’s really about connection. When you hear better, you connect to the world. It reduces dementia risk and depression risk,” he continued.

“There’s impactful hearing health factors associated with better hearing. We’ve got a product that lives on people for 16 hours that is trusted to help them with their hearing and their vision, and we’d love to continue helping them in every way we can.”

When the frames launch later this year, Legato says they’ll be available through select eye-care providers nationwide and will “cost a fraction” of traditional hearing aids and may be eligible for vision insurance when purchased through an eye-care clinic.
